class.name: BoxImpostorBaker
class.brief_description: Bakes a model into a box impostor: its bounding box with what the model looks like from each side (Mariner G5b).
class.description: A box impostor draws a model seen from far away (a building, a warehouse, a quay, a ship at anchor) as its bounding box, a dozen triangles. Every face of the box carries what an orthographic camera saw of the model from that side - the color, the normals and the depth of the relief below the face - and the material's deep parallax in impostor mode ([member BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_impostor]) traces the view ray into that relief: the right parallax and silhouette from any angle, the relief's depth for intersections and the sun's shadow maps, and the light, wetness, fog and windows of an ordinary [StandardMaterial3D]. [method bake] photographs a copy of the source (without scripts) in a viewport of its own, five sides (six with [member bake_bottom]), and packs the faces into a square atlas at one texel density, so that one relief scale serves every face. Bake with the Forward+ renderer (Mobile: materials other than [BaseMaterial3D] are baked lit; Compatibility: LDR colors); the impostor is drawn by every renderer. [codeblock] var baker = BoxImpostorBaker.new() baker.texels_per_meter = 8.0 var mesh = baker.bake($Warehouse) ResourceSaver.save(mesh, "res://warehouse_impostor.res") [/codeblock] In the editor: select the model's root node and use [b]Project > Tools > Bake Box Impostor[/b]; the mesh is saved next to the scene and added as a sibling [MeshInstance3D]. Switch between the model and its impostor with the visibility ranges of [GeometryInstance3D] (for example the model to 300 m, the impostor from 300 m with a fade). With [member hull] (the default) the ray is traced against all the faces' reliefs at once (the visual hull of the five views): inner corners and walls seen edge-on by one face are right. Still, a hollow no face sees into (a courtyard closed on four sides, a recess under a roof) is filled in.

method.name: bake
method.description: Bakes [param source] (a [Node3D] inside the scene tree with its visible geometry below it) into a box impostor: a mesh with one surface (the box's faces, each with its rectangle of the atlas in [constant Mesh.ARRAY_CUSTOM0]) and its [StandardMaterial3D] (albedo, normal map, height map in impostor mode with the depth offset; [member BaseMaterial3D.interior_mask_texture] where the source has transparent glass). Returns [code]null[/code] if the source has no visible geometry. Renders several frames at once ([method RenderingServer.force_draw]): call it from the main thread, not while a frame is being drawn.

method.name: get_albedo_image
method.description: The last bake's color atlas (sRGB, alpha: the model's coverage).

method.name: get_atlas_meters
method.description: The side of the last bake's atlas in meters (the atlas is square, at one texel density).

method.name: get_height_image
method.description: The last bake's relief atlas: [code]1[/code] on a face, [code]0[/code] at [method get_relief_depth] below it or where nothing is.

method.name: get_normal_image
method.description: The last bake's normal map atlas (tangent space of the impostor's faces).

method.name: get_relief_depth
method.description: The depth of the last bake's relief in meters: the box's largest side and 2 percent.

method.name: get_window_image
method.description: The last bake's window mask (the source's surfaces with transparent materials), or [code]null[/code] if it has none.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the bottom face is baked too (for models seen from below: a bridge, a ship's hull).

If [code]true[/code], the material traces the visual hull of all the faces' reliefs ([member BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_impostor_faces], Mariner G5c): right inner corners and walls seen edge-on by a face. If [code]false[/code], each face traces its own relief (cheaper, wrong in inner corners).
The largest side of the atlas in texels: when the faces do not fit at [member texels_per_meter], the density is lowered.
Texels around each face in the atlas (filled with the face's edge colors, so that filtering and mipmaps do not bleed).
The atlas's texel density. At 300 m a 1920 x 1080 view at 60 degrees shows about 3 pixels per meter.
